title: H224: Fix the missing Q.922 header in H.224 dissector
description:
Resolve the missing three bytes of Q.922 header in H.224 dissector.
Fixs #18655

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 8679839c - H224:Fix the missing Q.922 header in H.224 dissector
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8918/diffs?diff_id=539291131&start_sha=af8a1cc84cb987c12a996cef13297664c3a27df2)

@easonweii 
Is it possible to split the header into bits to isolate the priority?
```
######################Q.922 header######################
000000   DLCI HI        --- always 0
      0 C/R             --- always 0
       0 EA             --- always 0
0110     DLCI LO (0x06) --- may be 0x06 (Low priority) or 0x07 (High priority)
    0    FECN           --- always 0
     0   BECN           --- always 0
      0  DE             --- always 0
       1 EA             --- always 1

```
you want to show the priority separately?

Yes, because all other bits always have the same value, and the priority bits can change, one could read them as a priority separately. Or you can just display the value as a priority in the text view.
Only one octet used in this mode. I think, it's should be "Q.922 Control Octet"
changed this line in version 2 of the diff

The bits of the data priority can be directly displayed, more clearer.

Maybe, then add logic like this:
```
if hf_h224_q922_dlci_priority == (0000000110 (upper DLCI 0x00, lower DLCI 0x06)) 
    then print "Low priority data" 
else 
if hf_h224_q922_dlci_priority == (0000000111 (upper DLCI 0x00, lower DLCI 0x07)) 
    then print "High priority data" 
else 
    print bits
```
Good suggestion,will done.

Originally, the priority data is calculated and then displayed. This is because the 10-bit field is a combination of the Upper DLCI and Lower DLCI fields. When the values of the Upper DLCI fields are all 0, there is no problem. In fact, the protocol also defines this rule. Thanks your review.
